4867.title: React Element
4867.heading: React Element
4867.content:
A React element is an object describing what should appear at one position in the interface tree. JSX expressions produce these element descriptions for intrinsic browser elements or for other React components.

Elements are descriptions rather than mutable document nodes. React compares the newly produced tree with the prior rendering and applies the required browser updates.

4870.title: React Context
4870.heading: React Context
4870.content:
React context passes a value through a component subtree without forwarding it through every intermediate component's props. A provider establishes the value, and descendants beneath that provider can consume it.

Context is useful for closely related shared concerns such as form values and handlers or authentication state. It does not make all state global; provider placement defines the boundary of access.

4873.content:
Razor-and-blades pricing discounts or gives away a base component and earns revenue from the recurring service or consumable required to make it useful. A connected device can be inexpensive while its cloud storage, analysis, or monitoring carries the ongoing charge.

The model shifts attention from the acquisition price to the total dependency between components. A consumer should evaluate the continuing service price and the consequences of switching before treating the subsidized component as inexpensive.

4891.title: Rayleigh Quotient
4891.heading: Rayleigh Quotient
4891.content:
For a nonzero vector $x$ and square matrix $A$, the Rayleigh quotient is $R(x)=x^TAx/(x^Tx)$. If $x$ is an eigenvector, the quotient equals its eigenvalue.

Applied to an approximate eigenvector, it supplies an eigenvalue estimate. For a symmetric matrix its values are bounded by the smallest and largest eigenvalues.

4894.title: Rayleigh Criterion
4894.heading: Rayleigh Criterion
4894.content: The Rayleigh criterion says that two point sources are just resolved when the central diffraction maximum of one coincides with the first minimum of the other. For a circular aperture, the limiting angle is approximately $1.22\lambda/D$. Larger apertures and shorter wavelengths therefore resolve finer angular detail.

4897.title: Ray Casting
4897.heading: Ray Casting
4897.content:
Ray casting tests a half-line defined by an origin and direction against collision geometry. The result can identify whether an intersection occurs and the parameter or point at which the first hit is found.

Games use ray casts for visibility, weapon traces, camera obstruction, audio obstruction, and [[Object Picking]]. The direction should be normalized when distance is meant to correspond directly to the ray parameter.

A raw Ethernet storage protocol places storage-specific messages directly in Ethernet frames instead of passing every request through a full general-purpose network stack. The shorter path can reduce processing, copies, and latency for small I/O.

The protocol must supply any required reliability, addressing, flow control, and request matching that higher layers would otherwise provide.

The book uses body mass index, calculated from weight and height, to illustrate how a combined measure may relate more strongly to a study target than either input alone.

Derived features still need domain scrutiny. A useful calculation for one setting may be unhelpful elsewhere, and an inappropriate transformation can hide differences. Feature design is part of representing the problem, not just a technical optimization after data collection.

For an integer polynomial, every rational root in lowest terms has numerator dividing the constant coefficient and denominator dividing the leading coefficient. This produces a finite list of candidates.

Failure of every candidate can prove a quadratic or cubic irreducible over the rationals.

4909.title: Rational Number
4909.heading: Rational Number
4909.content:
A rational number is a number expressible as a quotient of two integers,

$$\frac{a}{b},\qquad b\neq0.$$

Rational numbers include integers and positive or negative [[Fraction]]s. They are closed under addition, subtraction, and multiplication, and under division by a nonzero rational number. In positional decimal notation, every rational number has an expansion that either terminates or eventually repeats. Conversely, a terminating or [[Repeating Decimal]] represents a rational number.

4912.title: Rational Inequality
4912.heading: Rational Inequality
4912.content: A rational inequality compares a [[Rational Expression]] with zero or another expression. Zeros of the numerator and denominator divide the number line into sign intervals, but denominator zeros are always excluded. A sign chart avoids unsafe cross-multiplication by a quantity whose sign may be unknown.

4915.title: Rational Implicitization
4915.heading: Rational Implicitization
4915.content:
Rational implicitization converts coordinate ratios fᵢ/gᵢ into polynomial equations for the closure of the parametrized image. The construction must exclude parameter values where a denominator vanishes.

Auxiliary variables and equations enforce the nonvanishing condition before a [[Gröbner Basis]] eliminates parameters. The resulting relations describe the image without retaining the original parameter coordinates.

4918.title: Rational Function
4918.heading: Rational Function
4918.content: A rational function is a quotient $f(x)=p(x)/q(x)$ of polynomials with $q(x)\ne0$. Zeros of the denominator are excluded from its domain and may produce holes or [[Vertical Asymptote]]s. Comparing polynomial degrees helps determine end behavior and possible [[Horizontal Asymptote]]s.

4921.title: Rational Expression
4921.heading: Rational Expression
4921.content:
A rational expression is a quotient of algebraic expressions, commonly polynomials:

$$\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)},\qquad Q(x)\neq0.$$

It generalizes a numerical [[Fraction]] while retaining the restriction that its denominator cannot be zero. Operations follow fraction rules, but polynomial factorization is often required before cancellation or construction of a common denominator. Equivalent-looking simplified forms must preserve the original excluded values because cancelling a factor does not make the original denominator defined there.

4924.heading: Ratio Cut Relaxation
4924.content:
Ratio cut measures a graph partition by summing the cut weight for each group after dividing by the number of vertices in that group. The balance term penalizes solutions that create tiny isolated clusters.

Optimizing the discrete objective exactly is difficult. A spectral relaxation replaces discrete membership indicators with continuous vectors, solves an eigenvector problem, and then rounds the embedding back to cluster assignments.

4927.title: Rational Exponent
4927.heading: Rational Exponent
4927.content: A rational exponent connects powers and roots: $a^{m/n}=(\sqrt[n]{a})^m$ when the real root is defined. The denominator selects the root and the numerator selects the power. These definitions extend the [[Exponent Laws]], but even roots impose nonnegative-radicand restrictions when calculations remain in the real numbers.

4930.title: Rater Policy
4930.heading: Rater Policy
4930.content:
A rater policy is the functional relationship a judge appears to use when converting a profile of predictor values into an overall decision. Judgmental analysis represents that relationship through a multiple-regression equation.

Comparing equations reveals whether judges share a policy even when their individual ratings differ. The result preserves both the direction and relative importance of the predictors.

4933.heading: Rate and Displacement Gyroscopes
4933.content: A displacement gyro indicates an angular position such as pitch, roll, or heading, while a rate gyro indicates angular change per unit time. A restricted single-gimbal rate gyro can support turn indication, whereas freer gyros provide stable attitude or directional references. Pneumatic or electric power keeps the rotor spinning, but each installation introduces characteristic limits and errors.

4936.title: RasterStack
4936.heading: RasterStack
4936.content: A `RasterStack` is a collection of raster layers that share compatible extent and resolution but may remain separate data sources. It provides one object for selecting, plotting, and calculating across variables or times. A `RasterBrick` stores a truly multilayer raster more compactly and can be more efficient, whereas a stack is flexible for combining files. A time index can turn either representation into a [[Time-Indexed Raster Stack]].

Each slice is a spatial snapshot, so comparing slices reveals movement or change without mixing cells from different times. A few slices can be shown as small multiples, while a long sequence may require [[Monthly Raster Aggregation]] or animation. Shared color limits are necessary for magnitude comparison across slices.

A layer may represent a quantitative field such as elevation or categorical classes such as land cover. Cell size determines spatial resolution, while extent and [[Coordinate Reference System]] locate the grid. Multiple aligned layers can form a [[RasterStack]] for different variables or times.

4957.content:
Rare class stream detection identifies a known minority class within a continuous flow where recent windows contain few positive examples. Ordinary accuracy can remain high even when the stream classifier misses every rare event.

Costs, selective sampling, class-sensitive thresholds, and protected memory can increase attention to the minority. The learner must distinguish a persistent rare class from a genuinely new class whose first cases were absent from training.

4960.content:
Rare class learning develops a classifier when one important class has far fewer labeled examples than the others. Standard error minimization can favor the majority because misclassifying all rare cases contributes little to overall accuracy.

Costs, weights, resampling, ensembles, one-class models, and specialized evaluation measures redirect attention toward minority detection. The correct choice depends on whether the rare class is known, partially labeled, or genuinely novel.

The threshold should be reported because aggregation trades detail for readability and may hide a small but important group.

4966.title: Rapid Elasticity
4966.heading: Rapid Elasticity
4966.content:
Rapid elasticity is the ability to add resources when demand rises and release them when demand falls. It uses [[Horizontal Scalability]] in both directions so that capacity can follow a changing workload instead of remaining fixed at its anticipated peak.

Elasticity depends on [[Resource Pooling]], automation, and sufficiently fast provisioning. It can protect service availability during a surge and reduce idle capacity afterward, but it does not remove the need to measure workload behavior or set safe scaling rules.

4969.title: Ransomware
4969.heading: Ransomware
4969.content:
Ransomware denies access to data or systems and demands payment for restoration. It commonly encrypts files, but the coercive objective can also involve locking systems or threatening to disclose stolen information.

The attack can harm [[Cybersecurity Availability]] and [[Cybersecurity Confidentiality]] at the same time. Reliable isolated backups, restricted privileges, patching, filtering, network segmentation, and practiced recovery reduce both the opportunity for infection and the attacker's leverage.

4972.title: RANSAC
4972.heading: RANSAC
4972.content:
RANSAC is a robust estimation procedure that repeatedly fits a model from a small random sample and counts how many observations agree with it. The candidate with a strong consensus set can be refined using those inliers while rejecting outliers.

In AR pose estimation, this prevents a modest number of incorrect feature matches from dominating the camera solution. Its success depends on enough correct matches, a suitable error threshold, and enough trials to sample a useful subset.

4975.title: Ranking Prediction
4975.heading: Ranking Prediction
4975.content:
Ranking prediction orders items by expected popularity, influence, or relevance instead of estimating an exact value. Evaluation must consider both whether relevant items appear and how highly they are placed.

Metrics such as [[Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain]] support graded relevance, while [[Average Precision]] is useful when relevance is binary. The metric should reflect the positions users or decisions actually inspect.

4978.heading: Rank of a Module Homomorphism
4978.content:
For a homomorphism represented by a matrix A and an R-module M, the rank on M is the largest r for which the ideal generated by the r-by-r minors of A is not contained in Ann(M).

This determinantal definition works over rings where ordinary row reduction is insufficient. Rank conditions combine with depth of minor ideals in the [[Buchsbaum-Eisenbud Exactness Criterion]].

4981.title: Randomized Algorithm
4981.heading: Randomized Algorithm
4981.content:
A randomized algorithm deliberately uses chance when selecting part of its execution path. Its result or runtime can vary between runs even when the input is unchanged.

Randomness can avoid consistently unfavorable deterministic choices. [[Quicksort]] selects pivots randomly so that its expected complexity is loglinear, even though a theoretically possible sequence of extreme pivots would be much slower. Correct sorting is guaranteed; chance affects performance rather than correctness.

4984.title: Randomization
4984.heading: Randomization
4984.content:
Randomization selects among outcomes using apparent chance, through devices such as dice, shuffled cards, or software-generated values. Perfect physical randomness is unnecessary when the result is functionally unpredictable to players.

Games use randomization to represent detail below the chosen modeling level and to create uncertainty. The resulting probabilities must still support perceived fairness, because players often judge short sequences by intuition rather than by statistical expectation.

In scene design, chance is most useful for generating combinations among already meaningful rules. It can prevent memorization, break stagnation, and force competitors away from symmetrical strategies, but it is not a substitute for designing strong interactions.

4987.title: Random-Projection Seriation
4987.heading: Random-Projection Seriation
4987.content:
Seriation gives observations a one-dimensional order that may serve as a starting point for hierarchy construction. The book takes several random projections and averages them; in its tested settings, this consensus correlates closely with row marginal sums.

A direct marginal sum is cheap, but distinct vectors can share it. A projection can separate some such ties while retaining a simple scalar representation. Neither order is guaranteed to be the unique or optimal hierarchy, so the subsequent tree and its proximity behavior need comparison with the original multivariate data.

4990.title: Random Variable
4990.heading: Random Variable
4990.content:
A random variable assigns a numerical value to the outcome of a random process. Its realized value changes across repeated samples or experiments even when the underlying population and procedure remain fixed.

The source treats sample means, mean differences, test statistics, and p-values as random variables. Recognizing this variability is essential because an observed estimate is one realization from a [[Sampling Distribution]], not the population quantity itself.

4993.title: Random System
4993.heading: Random System
4993.content:
A random system produces outcomes that are not determined in advance, although they may fall within a defined probability range. Its unpredictability comes from chance rather than from sensitivity in a deterministic rule set.

This distinguishes it from a [[Chaotic System]]. Games use [[Randomization]] to stand in for systems that are too detailed to model and to introduce uncertainty into [[Meaningful Decision|meaningful decisions]].

At a [[Dangling Node]], the surfer can jump to any page. The fuller model also permits [[PageRank Teleportation]] from ordinary pages with a chosen probability, preventing the surfer from becoming trapped in a [[Link Sink]].

5002.content:
Random projection maps a high-dimensional vector onto one or a few lower-dimensional axes. The projected value can then be quantized into a prefix bin, making projection plus longest-common-prefix matching a similarity-oriented hashing method.

Nearby vectors may land in the same bin, allowing candidate matches to be found without comparing every original pair. Projection and quantization can also cause collisions or separate genuine neighbors, so the book tests stability and compares resulting groups with other methods. The hash is an approximate search aid, not an exact equality test on the original vectors.

5008.heading: Random Forest Classification
5008.content:
Random forest classification combines decision trees trained on bootstrap samples while considering a random subset of features at each split. Both sources of randomness promote diversity among the trees.

The final class is chosen by aggregate voting. Deep individual trees can fit complex patterns, while averaging reduces their variance; restricting candidate features prevents a few dominant predictors from making every tree too similar.

The book fits hundreds of randomized trees, monitors [[Out-of-Bag Error]], and examines variable importance before evaluating held-out probabilities. The gap between near-perfect training performance and weaker validation performance remains evidence that ensemble accuracy must be checked independently.

5017.content:

The index can rise as the number of clusters increases and does not correct for chance agreement. Adjusted variants address those limitations.

5023.title: Radix Sort
5023.heading: Radix Sort
5023.content:
Radix sort orders records by distributing them according to successive parts of their keys. Beginning with the least significant digit or character, it places items into ordered buckets, collects the buckets without disturbing their internal order, and repeats for the next position.

For $n$ keys of width $w$, its complexity is $O(nw)$. Because it treats even numerical keys as sequences of symbols rather than comparing their complete values, it is a [[String Sorting]] method.

5035.title: Radioactive Tracer
5035.heading: Radioactive Tracer
5035.content: A radioactive tracer is an isotope incorporated into a biologically active substance so its distribution can be detected outside the body. The tracer should emit sufficiently penetrating radiation, have a half-life long enough for the procedure but short enough to limit dose, and participate in the process under investigation without substantially altering it.

5038.title: Radioactive Decay
5038.heading: Radioactive Decay
5038.content: Radioactive decay is a spontaneous, random nuclear transformation. The time of one nucleus's decay cannot be predicted, but a large population follows $N=N_0e^{-\lambda t}$ with constant decay probability per unit time. Activity is $A=\lambda N$, so it falls with the same exponential law.

Satellite navigation preserves the idea of broadcast time while using higher-frequency signals and explicit corrections for propagation delay.

5044.heading: Radical of an Ideal
5044.content:
The radical √I of an [[Ideal]] I consists of all ring elements r for which some positive power rⁿ lies in I. It is itself an ideal and equals the intersection of all [[Prime Ideal]]s containing I.

Taking a radical removes information about powers while preserving the same prime support. An ideal equal to its radical is a [[Radical Ideal]], and the radical of the zero ideal is the [[Nilradical]].

5065.title: Race Condition
5065.heading: Race Condition
5065.content:
A race condition occurs when a program's result depends on the timing or interleaving of concurrent operations. Unsynchronized read-modify-write sequences can lose updates even when each individual read and write appears simple.

Races are prevented by removing shared mutable state, partitioning ownership, using immutable data, or applying an appropriate synchronization primitive. Tests may fail to reproduce them consistently because scheduling changes from run to run.

The design-patterns source demonstrates that making an inventory context a singleton does not make `Quantity += amount` atomic. Two threads can read the same old quantity and overwrite one another's updates. Locking the read-modify-write section protects that invariant, while constructing the singleton itself needs a separate one-time creation guarantee.

5086.title: R Package
5086.heading: R Package
5086.content:
An R package is a distributable collection of functions, data, and documentation that extends base R. Packages let analysts assemble the capabilities required for a project instead of installing one monolithic statistical program with every possible component.

Published packages on CRAN follow documentation requirements and can be installed without licensing fees. Their flexibility creates a maintenance obligation, because a package may depend on other packages and may evolve independently of the R version used in production.

Installation and loading are separate operations: `install.packages` places a package on the system, while `library` attaches it to the current R session. This distinction lets an analysis declare the packages it uses without reinstalling them on every run.

The book further distinguishes installing a package from making it available in a session. [[R Library Attachment]] exposes exported functions on the search path, while an explicit [[R Package Namespace]] can identify the provider without attaching it.

R data import converts an external data file or resource into an R object such as an [[R Data Frame]]. The source uses `read.csv` with either a local path or a URL and stresses that the analyst must know which file and location the command addresses.

An import step should remain explicit and reproducible. File format, header interpretation, variable classes, and missing values must be checked before later transformations or models are trusted.

The book uses explicit readers such as `read_csv` and then assigns the result to a stable working object. Import remains only the first step: [[Dataset Dimension Review]], [[Dataset Glimpse]], and class correction establish whether the table is analytically usable.

5113.title: R Data Frame
5113.heading: R Data Frame
5113.content:
An R data frame is a rectangular object whose columns represent variables and whose rows represent observations. Different columns may have different classes, while every column must align to the same set of rows.

Data frames are the principal R objects for health-data analysis. Analysts can select columns, subset rows, add recoded variables, pass the object into functions, and create revised copies as checkpoints. This object-centered workflow differs from the implicit row loop of the [[SAS Data Step]].

The life-science workflow in the source imports delimited tables as data frames and then uses dplyr operations to select variables and filter experimental groups. Row and column alignment makes the object a natural interface between raw observations, graphics, and statistical models.

The book treats the data frame as the main interface among imported records, cleaning operations, visualizations, and predictive models. Reviewing its dimensions, names, classes, and sample rows makes the transition from external resource to analytic object explicit.

5116.title: R Console
5116.heading: R Console
5116.content:
The R console is the interactive window in which commands execute and textual results, messages, warnings, and errors appear. Code may be typed directly or sent from an R script, while graphical output opens in a separate graphics device.

Because several kinds of output share the console, it is not automatically equivalent to a clean SAS log. Durable work should remain in scripts and documented objects; selected console evidence can be preserved when it helps explain an error or validate an analysis.

For an introductory R workflow, the console also serves as the immediate place to request function help, load packages, and test commands before preserving them in a reproducible project. The source treats console familiarity as a prerequisite for following its statistical examples.

In the book's RStudio workflow, the console provides immediate feedback while scripts preserve the analysis. Commands, warnings, and errors are inspected there, but repeatable work is moved into source files and functions.

5119.heading: R Data File Naming
5119.content:
R data file naming distinguishes serialized workspaces or objects from scripts and source data. Consistent extensions and lowercase descriptive names help tools and collaborators infer the file's role.

Generated data filenames should also encode versioning or provenance through the workflow rather than ad hoc renaming.
